}
tabs($("#vc-tabs"), VC_ARMS.map(function(a){ return a[1]; }), vcSel, function(i){ vcSel = i; drawVc(); });

/* ================================================================ 6. TRY IT */
(function(){
  var sel = $("#try-sent");
  SENTS.forEach(function(s, i){ var o = document.createElement("option"); o.value = String(i); var t = s.text.length > 90 ? s.text.slice(0, 88) + "…" : s.text; o.textContent = (i + 1) + ". " + t; sel.appendChild(o); });
  sel.value = String(exS);
  var box = $("#try-peers");
  SYS.forEach(function(sy, i){ var l = document.createElement("label"); l.innerHTML = '<input type="checkbox" checked value="' + i + '"> ' + esc(SHORT[sy]); box.appendChild(l); });
})();
function drawTry(){
  var si = +$("#try-sent").value, s = SENTS[si], uni = radioVal("try-w") === "uni";
  var active = $$("#try-peers input").filter(function(c){ return c.checked; }).map(function(c){ return +c.value; });
  var weights = {}; SYS.forEach(function(sy){ weights[sy] = uni ? 1 : W8[sy]; });
  var rows = [];
  for (var m = 0; m < 9; m++){ var it = itemFor(si, m); if (!it) continue; var sc = scoreOne(si, m, active, weights); rows.push({m:m, it:it, sc:sc}); }
  $("#try-sentence").innerHTML = '<strong>Sentence:</strong> ' + esc(s.text) + ' <span class="muted">(' + esc(CORPUS[s.corpus]) + '; audited gold <code>' + esc(s.gold || "none") + '</code>)</span>';
  var host = $("#chart-try"), W = widthOf(host), narrow = W < 520, labW = narrow ? 112 : 160, rowH = 30, H = rows.length * rowH + 44, x0 = labW, x1 = W - 20;
  var svg = newSvg(host, W, H, "Recomputed peer agreement score per output");
  var sx = function(v){ return x0 + (x1 - x0) * v; };
  var g = el("g", {"class":"axis"}, svg);
  [0, .25, .5, .75, 1].forEach(function(t){ el("line", {x1:sx(t), x2:sx(t), y1:2, y2:H - 30, "class":"gridline"}, g); txt(g, sx(t), H - 16, t.toFixed(2), {"text-anchor":"middle"}); });
  txt(g, (x0 + x1)/2, H - 1, "peer agreement score (recomputed)", {"text-anchor":"middle"});
  var match = 0, cmp = 0;
  rows.forEach(function(r, i){
    var y = 4 + i * rowH + rowH/2 - 4, col = r.it.ys === 1 ? "var(--good)" : (r.it.ys === 0 ? "var(--bad)" : "#9aa1ab");
    txt(svg, labW - 8, y + 4, SHORT[SYS[r.m]], {"text-anchor":"end", "font-size": narrow ? "11" : "12.5", fill: active.indexOf(r.m) < 0 ? "#8a929c" : "#1c2128"});
    el("line", {x1:x0, x2:x1, y1:y, y2:y, stroke:"#f0f1f3"}, svg);
    el("circle", {cx:sx(r.it.PA), cy:y, r:8, fill:"none", stroke:"#333", "stroke-width":1.6}, svg);
    var dot = el("circle", {cx:sx(r.sc.score), cy:y, r:5.5, fill:col}, svg);
    if (!r.it.ok) txt(svg, sx(r.sc.score) + 12, y + 4, "unparseable", {"font-size":"11", fill:"#59626e"});
    bindMark(dot, function(){ return "<b>" + esc(SYS[r.m]) + "</b><br>recomputed " + r.sc.score.toFixed(3) + (r.sc.covered ? "" : " (fewer than 2 covered peers: 0.5)") + "<br>recorded " + r.it.PA.toFixed(3) + "<br>solver label: " + (r.it.ys == null ? "none" : r.it.ys ? "faithful" : "unfaithful") + "<br><span style='font-family:monospace'>" + esc(r.it.f) + "</span>"; }, SYS[r.m] + " recomputed " + r.sc.score.toFixed(3));
    cmp++; if (Math.abs(r.sc.score - r.it.PA) < 1e-5) match++;
  });
  var full = active.length === 9 && !uni, miss = PEERS.rels[si].indexOf("?") >= 0, t;
  var fa = rows.filter(function(r){ return r.it.ys === 1; }), un = rows.filter(function(r){ return r.it.ys === 0; });
  var mean = function(a){ if (!a.length) return null; var s2 = 0; a.forEach(function(r){ s2 += r.sc.score; }); return s2 / a.length; };
  var mf = mean(fa), mu = mean(un);
  if (full) t = "All nine systems count as peers with fitted weights: the recomputed score equals the recorded one for " + match + " of " + cmp + " outputs" + (miss ? " (this sentence has pairs missing from the saved cache, which explains any difference)." : ".");
  else t = (uni ? "Uniform weights" : "Fitted weights") + " with " + active.length + " of 9 systems as peers: " + (cmp - match) + " of " + cmp + " scores differ from the recorded run.";
  if (mf != null && mu != null) t += " Faithful outputs average " + mf.toFixed(3) + " and unfaithful ones " + mu.toFixed(3) + ".";
  $("#try-take").textContent = t;
}
$("#try-sent").addEventListener("change", drawTry);
$$("input[name='try-w']").forEach(function(r){ r.addEventListener("change", drawTry); });
$("#try-peers").addEventListener("change", drawTry);

/* ---- flag budget */
function budgetCurve(key, fam){
  var rows = ITEMS.filter(function(r){ return (fam === "panel" ? r.yp : r.ys) != null; });
  var W = 0, U = 0;
  rows.forEach(function(r){ var w = fam === "panel" ? r.w : 1, y = fam === "panel" ? r.yp : r.ys; W += w; if (y === 0) U += w; });
  rows.sort(function(a, b){ return a[key] - b[key]; });
  var groups = [], i = 0;
  while (i < rows.length){ var j = i, gw = 0, gu = 0, v = rows[i][key];
    while (j < rows.length && rows[j][key] === v){ var w = fam === "panel" ? rows[j].w : 1, y = fam === "panel" ? rows[j].yp : rows[j].ys; gw += w; if (y === 0) gu += w; j++; }
    groups.push({w:gw, u:gu}); i = j; }
  return function(share){
    var target = share * W, got = 0, bad = 0;
    for (var k = 0; k < groups.length && got < target - 1e-9; k++){
      var take = Math.min(1, (target - got) / groups[k].w);
      got += take * groups[k].w; bad += take * groups[k].u;
    }
    return {prec: bad / got, rec: bad / U, base: U / W};
  };
}
function drawBudget(){
  var fam = radioVal("bud-label"), b = +$("#bud").value / 100;
  $("#bud-val").textContent = Math.round(b * 100) + "%";
  var cp = budgetCurve("PA", fam), cj = budgetCurve("J", fam);
  var host = $("#chart-bud"), W = widthOf(host), H = 280, ml = 52, mr = 18, mt = 12, mb = 44;
  var s = newSvg(host, W, H, "Share of flagged outputs that are unfaithful, by review budget");
  var sx = function(v){ return ml + (W - ml - mr) * (v - .05) / .55; }, sy = function(v){ return mt + (H - mt - mb) * (1 - v); };
  var g = el("g", {"class":"axis"}, s);
  [0, .25, .5, .75, 1].forEach(function(t){ el("line", {x1:ml, x2:W - mr, y1:sy(t), y2:sy(t), "class":"gridline"}, g); txt(g, ml - 6, sy(t) + 4, pct(t, 0), {"text-anchor":"end"}); });
  [.05, .2, .4, .6].forEach(function(t){ txt(g, sx(t), H - mb + 16, pct(t, 0), {"text-anchor":"middle"}); });
  txt(g, (ml + W - mr)/2, H - 6, "share of outputs flagged (lowest scores first)", {"text-anchor":"middle"});
  var yl = txt(g, 12, (mt + H - mb)/2, "precision: flagged that are unfaithful", {"text-anchor":"middle", transform:"rotate(-90 12 " + (mt + H - mb)/2 + ")"});
  var base = cp(.2).base;
  el("line", {x1:ml, x2:W - mr, y1:sy(base), y2:sy(base), stroke:"#777", "stroke-dasharray":"4 3"}, s);
  txt(s, W - mr - 4, sy(base) - 5, "base rate " + pct(base, 1), {"text-anchor":"end", "font-size":"11.5", fill:"#59626e"});
  [[cp, "var(--accent)", "Peer agreement"], [cj, "var(--base)", "LLM judge"]].forEach(function(c){
    var d = ""; for (var p = 5; p <= 60; p++){ var v = c[0](p / 100).prec; d += (p === 5 ? "M" : "L") + sx(p / 100).toFixed(1) + " " + sy(v).toFixed(1); }
    el("path", {d:d, fill:"none", stroke:c[1], "stroke-width":2.4}, s);
    var cur = c[0](b), dot = el("circle", {cx:sx(b), cy:sy(cur.prec), r:6, fill:c[1], stroke:"#fff", "stroke-width":1.5}, s);
    bindMark(dot, "<b>" + c[2] + "</b><br>flag " + pct(b, 0) + "<br>precision " + pct(cur.prec) + "<br>recall of unfaithful " + pct(cur.rec), c[2] + " precision " + pct(cur.prec));
  });
  el("line", {x1:sx(b), x2:sx(b), y1:mt, y2:H - mb, stroke:"#1c2128", "stroke-width":1, "stroke-dasharray":"2 3"}, s);
  var P = cp(b), Q = cj(b);
  $("#bud-take").textContent = "Flagging the lowest " + pct(b, 0) + " under " + (fam === "panel" ? "weighted panel" : "solver") + " labels: " + pct(P.prec) + " of the outputs peer agreement flags are unfaithful (catching " + pct(P.rec) + " of all unfaithful), against " + pct(Q.prec) + " for the judge (catching " + pct(Q.rec) + "). The base rate is " + pct(P.base) + ".";
}
$("#bud").addEventListener("input", drawBudget);
$$("input[name='bud-label']").forEach(function(r){ r.addEventListener("change", drawBudget); });

/* ================================================================ 7. DOSE */
function drawDose(){
  var order = radioVal("dose-order"), k = +$("#dose-k").value, pts = E4.dose[order];
  $("#dose-kval").textContent = String(k);
  var host = $("#chart-dose"), W = widthOf(host), H = 260, ml = 48, mr = 16, mt = 12, mb = 44;
  var s = newSvg(host, W, H, "Detection by number of peers replaced");
  var sx = function(v){ return ml + (W - ml - mr) * v / 8; }, sy = function(v){ return mt + (H - mt - mb) * (1 - v); };
  var g = el("g", {"class":"axis"}, s);
  [0, .25, .5, .75, 1].forEach(function(t){ el("line", {x1:ml, x2:W - mr, y1:sy(t), y2:sy(t), "class":"gridline"}, g); txt(g, ml - 6, sy(t) + 4, t.toFixed(2), {"text-anchor":"end"}); });
  [0, 2, 4, 6, 8].forEach(function(t){ txt(g, sx(t), H - mb + 16, String(t), {"text-anchor":"middle"}); });
  txt(g, (ml + W - mr)/2, H - 6, "k = peers replaced by renamed copies of the mutant (of 8)", {"text-anchor":"middle"});
  txt(g, 12, (mt + H - mb)/2, "detection", {"text-anchor":"middle", transform:"rotate(-90 12 " + (mt + H - mb)/2 + ")"});
  el("line", {x1:ml, x2:W - mr, y1:sy(.5), y2:sy(.5), stroke:"#777", "stroke-dasharray":"4 3"}, s);
  var d = ""; pts.forEach(function(p, i){ d += (i ? "L" : "M") + sx(p.k) + " " + sy(p.pooled); });
  el("path", {d:d, fill:"none", stroke:"var(--accent)", "stroke-width":2.2}, s);
  pts.forEach(function(p){
    el("line", {x1:sx(p.k), x2:sx(p.k), y1:sy(p.ci[0]), y2:sy(p.ci[1]), stroke:"var(--accent)", "stroke-width":1.5}, s);
    var c = el("circle", {cx:sx(p.k), cy:sy(p.pooled), r: p.k === k ? 8 : 5, fill: p.k === k ? "var(--accent)" : "#fff", stroke:"var(--accent)", "stroke-width":2}, s);
    bindMark(c, "<b>k = " + p.k + "</b><br>detection " + f3(p.pooled) + " [" + f3(p.ci[0]) + ", " + f3(p.ci[1]) + "]<br>" + p.n + " items<br>drop conj. " + f3(p.ops.DROP_CONJ) + ", add conj. " + f3(p.ops.ADD_CONJ) + ",<br>∀/∃ " + f3(p.ops.QUANT) + ", impl. rev. " + f3(p.ops.IMPL_REV), "k " + p.k + " detection " + f3(p.pooled));
  });
  var cur = pts.filter(function(p){ return p.k === k; })[0];
  $("#dose-take").textContent = "With " + k + " of 8 peers replaced (" + (order === "random" ? "random order" : "faithful peers first") + "), the faithful formula outranks the mutant with probability " + f3(cur.pooled) + (cur.pooled < .5 ? ": most peer weight now sits on the error, so agreement prefers it." : ".") + " The observed curve equals the one predicted from peer weight alone at every k.";
}
$$("input[name='dose-order']").forEach(function(r){ r.addEventListener("change", drawDose); });
$("#dose-k").addEventListener("input", drawDose);

/* ---- real concordance */
function drawReal(){
  var lab = {"[0,0.25)":"< 25%", "[0.25,0.5)":"25–50%", "[0.5,0.75)":"50–75%", "[0.75,1.0)":"≥ 75%"};
  hbar($("#chart-real"), E4.real.map(function(r){ return {label:"wrong-meaning weight " + lab[r.bin], v:r.mean, ci:r.ci, color: r.mean < .6 ? "var(--bad)" : "var(--accent)",
    tip:"<b>" + lab[r.bin] + " of peer weight on wrong meanings</b><br>concordance " + f3(r.mean) + " [" + f3(r.ci[0]) + ", " + f3(r.ci[1]) + "]<br>" + fmtInt(r.pairs) + " pairs in " + r.sents + " sentences"}; }),
    {label:"Concordance within sentences by wrong-meaning peer weight", xlabel:"concordance within sentences (0.5 = coin flip)", labW: widthOf($("#chart-real")) < 520 ? 150 : 230});
  $("#real-take").textContent = "Concordance falls from " + f3(E4.real[0].mean) + " when wrong-meaning clusters hold under a quarter of the peer weight to " + f3(E4.real[3].mean) + " when they hold three quarters or more; the logistic slope is " + E4.slope.toFixed(2) + " [" + E4.slope_ci[0].toFixed(2) + ", " + E4.slope_ci[1].toFixed(2) + "].";
}

/* ---- legal */
var LG = [["all", "All (655 items)"], ["0-1", "0–1 markers"], ["2-3", "2–3 markers"], ["4+", "4+ markers"]];
var LG_M = [["PA", "Peer agreement", "var(--accent)"], ["MAJ", "Majority clustering", "var(--other)"], ["NLI", "Roundtrip NLI (L)", "var(--other)"], ["J", "LLM judge (flash)", "var(--base)"], ["FJ", "Frontier judge (pro)", "var(--base)"]];
var lgSel = 0;
function drawLegal(){
  var key = LG[lgSel][0], src = key === "all" ? LEGAL.all : LEGAL.bins[key];
  var n = key === "all" ? LEGAL.n : src.PA.n, pos = key === "all" ? LEGAL.pos : src.PA.pos;
  hbar($("#chart-legal"), LG_M.map(function(m){ var v = src[m[0]]; return {label:m[1], v:v.auc, ci:v.ci, color:m[2], bold:m[0] === "PA" || m[0] === "J",
    tip:"<b>" + esc(m[1]) + "</b><br>weighted AUROC " + f3(v.auc) + "<br>95% CI [" + f3(v.ci[0]) + ", " + f3(v.ci[1]) + "]<br>" + n + " items, " + pos + " faithful"}; }), {label:"Legal AUROC per score", labW: widthOf($("#chart-legal")) < 520 ? 128 : 160});
  var d = src.J.auc - src.PA.auc;
  $("#lg-take").textContent = (key === "all" ? "Across all 655 legal items" : "With " + LG[lgSel][1]) + ", peer agreement reaches " + f3(src.PA.auc) + " against the judge's " + f3(src.J.auc) + ", a deficit of " + d.toFixed(3) + "." + (pos < 10 ? " This bin holds only " + pos + " faithful items, so it supports no conclusion." : "");
}

/* ================================================================ TERMS + GLOSSARY */
var TERMS = {
  pa:["Peer agreement score", "The share, weighted by system reliability, of the other systems' formulas that an SMT solver proves logically equivalent to the candidate after a vocabulary alignment that never reads predicate names. Unparseable candidates, or those with fewer than two covered peers, receive 0.5."],
  auroc:["AUROC", "Area under the ROC curve: the probability that a randomly chosen faithful item scores above a randomly chosen unfaithful one (ties count one half). 0.5 is chance. Panel-label AUROC uses the sampling weights of the panel items."],
  panel:["Panel labels", "A panel of three LLMs (claude-haiku-4.5, grok-4.3, glm-4.6) sees the sentence with the gold and the candidate as two unnamed formulas in random order; the label is the majority of the three votes. 256 fresh items were labelled, weighted to match the sampling strata."],
  solver:["Audited solver labels", "The panel first audits each shipped gold. A candidate is faithful if the SMT solver proves it equivalent to the audited gold under an arity-preserving bijection of predicates and constants, searched without lexical information. 3,720 fresh rows."],
  ds:["Binary Dawid–Skene agreement", "A Dawid–Skene posterior with two classes over the same equivalence clusters, one of the latent-class agreement estimators the score is compared with."],
  ds1:["One-coin Dawid–Skene model", "A latent-class model with a single accuracy parameter per system, fitted over the equivalence clusters of all sentences without labels. It returns one reliability weight per system, floored at 0.05."],
  bij:["Bijection (alignment level 1)", "A one-to-one map of all predicates and constants of the peer onto those of the candidate that preserves arity. It is chosen by structure only."],
  partial:["Partial map (alignment level 2)", "An injective map that leaves some predicates of the peer unmatched, as fresh predicates, provided at least 50% of the peer's predicate occurrences are mapped. It admits peers that decompose a concept differently."],
  modal:["Modal cluster", "The equivalence cluster that carries the most peer weight for a sentence."],
  maj:["Majority equivalence clustering", "The share of other outputs in the candidate's cluster of outputs equivalent under a bijection, the selection mechanism of Li et al. (2024)."],
  vc:["Vocabulary conformity control", "The mean of the Jaccard overlap of predicate names with the peers and the agreement of arity profiles with the peers. It tests whether agreement merely rewards conventional names."],
  judge:["LLM judge", "gemini-2.5-flash, thinking off, temperature 0, asked for the probability that the formula is faithful to the sentence. The frontier judge is gemini-2.5-pro with the same prompt."],
  mutant:["Mutant", "A perturbed formula that is not logically equivalent to the gold, produced by an operator such as negation, an added or dropped conjunct, a ∀/∃ swap, implication reversal or an argument swap."],
  conc:["Concordance within sentences", "The probability that a faithful output scores above an unfaithful output of the same sentence."],
  gran:["Granularity definitions", "A further alignment level, left out of the frozen score, that lets one predicate stand for a conjunction of at most two literals of the other formula."],
  fresh:["Fresh set", "450 sentences from MALLS (170), the FOLIO v2 training split (150) and ProverQA (130), with zero string or story overlap with the 700 development sentences, formalized by nine LLMs: 4,050 greedy candidates, 222 of them unparseable and kept."]
};
var gl = $("#gloss");
Object.keys(TERMS).forEach(function(k){ var dt = document.createElement("dt"), dd = document.createElement("dd"); dt.textContent = TERMS[k][0]; dd.id = "def-" + k; dd.textContent = TERMS[k][1]; gl.appendChild(dt); gl.appendChild(dd); });
var tt = $("#termtip"), ttOwner = null;
function openTerm(b){
  var k = b.getAttribute("data-term"); if (!TERMS[k]) return;
  ttOwner = b; tt.innerHTML = "<strong>" + esc(TERMS[k][0]) + "</strong>" + esc(TERMS[k][1]); tt.classList.add("on");

aria-label=\"AUROC of each score for the selected labels and subset\"></div>\n        <ul class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\">\n          <li><i style=\"background:var(--accent)\"></i>Peer agreement</li>\n          <li><i style=\"background:var(--base)\"></i>LLM judge (baseline)</li>\n          <li><i style=\"background:var(--other)\"></i>Other scores</li>\n          <li><i style=\"background:none;border-left:2px dashed #888;border-radius:0;width:2px\"></i>Chance (0.5)</li>\n        </ul>\n        <p class=\"meta-line\" id=\"head-meta\"></p>\n        <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"head-take\"></p>\n      </div>\n      <p class=\"small muted\">AUROC is recomputed from the recorded scores at each change. Panel AUROC uses the raked sampling weights stored with each panel item. Roundtrip NLI exists only for 272 rows, so its bar uses its own n.</p>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============================ METHOD -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"method\" aria-labelledby=\"h-method\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-method\">How it works</h2>\n  <p class=\"question prose\"><strong>What happens to one real sentence?</strong> Step through how the score of one output is computed, with the relations, maps and weights the run recorded for this sentence.</p>\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"stepper\" aria-roledescription=\"stepper\">\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"pipe\" aria-label=\"Pipeline stages\"></div>\n    <div id=\"stage-live\" class=\"sr-only\" aria-live=\"polite\"></div>\n    <div class=\"stage-body\" id=\"stage-body\"></div>\n    <div class=\"stage-nav\">\n      <button class=\"plain\" id=\"st-prev\" type=\"button\">← Previous</button>\n      <button class=\"plain\" id=\"st-next\" type=\"button\">Next →</button>\n      <span class=\"stage-count\" id=\"st-count\"></span>\n      <span class=\"small muted\">Left and right arrow keys also move between stages.</span>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n  <figure>\n    <img src=\"figures/fig2_v0.jpg\" alt=\"Diagram of the peer agreement score: the candidate formula and eight peer formulas pass through name-free alignment (bijection, then partial map), a Z3 relation per pair (EQUIV, STRONGER, WEAKER, INCOMPARABLE, CONTRADICTORY, UNALIGNABLE), equivalence clusters with one-coin Dawid–Skene weights, and a weighted share of equivalent peers; the sentence itself is not read, and the gold can be scored as a tenth peer to flag wrong gold.\" width=\"1584\" height=\"672\" loading=\"lazy\">\n    <figcaption>The peer agreement score. A candidate formula is compared with each peer formula (other systems' outputs for the same sentence) after a vocabulary alignment that ignores predicate names (a bijection, then a partial map). An SMT solver decides the logical relation of each aligned pair. EQUIV relations define equivalence clusters, from which a Dawid–Skene model with one accuracy parameter per system, fitted without labels, estimates one reliability weight per system. The score is the weighted share of peers that are equivalent to the candidate. The sentence text and predicate names are never read.</figcaption>\n  </figure>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============================ EXPLORE -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"explore\" aria-labelledby=\"h-explore\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-explore\">Explore the evidence</h2>\n\n  <h3 id=\"h-browser\">Browse the 4,050 fresh outputs</h3>\n  <p class=\"question prose\"><strong>What does the score do to one case?</strong> Filter the fresh-set outputs, pick one, and read the sentence, the candidate, the audited gold, the score, the judge and both labels side by side.</p>\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-browser\">\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label class=\"ctl\"><span>Search sentence or formula</span><input type=\"search\" id=\"br-q\" placeholder=\"e.g. unless, HBO, ∃\"></label>\n      <label class=\"ctl\"><span>System</span><select id=\"br-sys\"><option value=\"\">All nine</option></select></label>\n      <label class=\"ctl\"><span>Corpus</span><select id=\"br-corpus\"><option value=\"\">All</option><option value=\"malls\">MALLS</option><option value=\"folio\">FOLIO</option><option <option value=\"panel\">Panel-labelled items (256)</option>\n          <option value=\"disagree\">Score and judge disagree</option>\n          <option value=\"missF\">Faithful (solver) but score below 0.5</option>\n          <option value=\"missU\">Unfaithful (solver) but score 0.5 or more</option>\n          <option value=\"modeBad\">Panel items where the modal cluster is unfaithful</option>\n          <option value=\"unparse\">Unparseable outputs</option>\n        </select></label>\n      <label class=\"ctl\"><span>Sort by</span>\n        <select id=\"br-sort\">\n          <option value=\"gap\">Largest score–judge gap</option>\n          <option value=\"paAsc\">Peer agreement, low to high</option>\n          <option value=\"paDesc\">Peer agreement, high to low</option>\n          <option value=\"jAsc\">Judge, low to high</option>\n          <option value=\"sent\">Sentence order</option>\n        </select></label>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"meta-line\" id=\"br-count\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    <div class=\"browser\">\n      <div>\n        <ul class=\"itemlist\" id=\"br-list\" aria-label=\"Matching outputs\"></ul>\n        <button class=\"plain\" id=\"br-more\" type=\"button\" style=\"margin-top:8px\">Show 40 more</button>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"detail\" id=\"br-detail\" aria-live=\"polite\"></div>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"br-take\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"two\">\n    <div>\n      <h3 id=\"h-complex\">Complexity strata</h3>\n      <p class=\"question\"><strong>Does the lead hold as sentences get harder?</strong> Panel-label AUROC of the score and the judge per stratum of one complexity feature.</p>\n      <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-complex\">\n        <div role=\"tablist\" aria-label=\"Complexity feature\" id=\"cx-tabs\"></div>\n        <div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-cx\"></div>\n        <ul class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><li><i style=\"background:var(--accent)\"></i>Peer agreement</li><li><i style=\"background:var(--base)\"></i>LLM judge</li></ul>\n        <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"cx-take\"></p>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n    <div>\n      <h3 id=\"h-vocab\">Vocabulary renderings</h3>\n      <p class=\"question\"><strong>Does the score just reward conventional names?</strong> The same faithful formulas and 739 operator mutants rendered four ways, on 223 development sentences (constructed truth).</p>\n      <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-vocab\">\n        <div role=\"tablist\" aria-label=\"Rendering\" id=\"vc-tabs\"></div>\n        <div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-vc\"></div>\n        <ul class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><li><i style=\"background:var(--accent)\"></i>Peer agreement (no granularity definitions)</li><li><i style=\"background:#5c8fc0\"></i>Majority clustering</li><li><i style=\"background:var(--base)\"></i>LLM judge</li><li><i style=\"background:var(--other)\"></i>Vocabulary conformity</li></ul>\n        <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"vc-take\"></p>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============================ TRY -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"try\" aria-labelledby=\"h-try\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-try\">Try it</h2>\n  <p class=\"question prose\"><strong>Can I run the score myself?</strong> Its last step is exact arithmetic over the recorded solver relations, so the page recomputes it. Pick any fresh sentence, remove peers or switch to uniform weights, and watch each output's score move. With all nine systems and the fitted weights, the recomputed score equals the recorded one.</p>\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-try\">\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label class=\"ctl\" style=\"flex:1 1 320px\"><span>Sentence</span><select id=\"try-sent\" style=\"width:100%\"></select></label>\n      <fieldset class=\"ctl\"><legend>System weights</legend>\n        <div class=\"seg\" id=\"try-w\">\n          <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"try-w\" value=\"ds\" checked><span>Fitted (Dawid–Skene)</span></label>\n          <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"try-w\" value=\"uni\"><span>Uniform</span></label>\n        </div>\n      </fieldset>\n    </div>\n    <fieldset class=\"ctl\" style=\"margin-bottom:10px\"><legend>Systems that count as peers</legend><div class=\"chk\" id=\"try-peers\"></div></fieldset>\n    <p class=\"small muted\" style=\"margin:0 0 8px\" id=\"try-sentence\"></p>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-try\"></div>\n    <ul class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><li><i style=\"background:var(--good)\"></i>Solver label faithful</li><li><i style=\"background:var(--bad)\"></i>Solver label unfaithful</li><li><i style=\"background:#9aa1ab\"></i>No solver label</li><li><i style=\"background:none;border:2px solid #333;border-radius:50%\"></i>Recorded score</li></ul>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"try-take\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <h3 id=\"h-budget\">What if you flag the lowest-scoring outputs?</h3>\n  <p class=\"question prose\"><strong>If I can only review a fixed share of outputs, which score picks better ones to review?</strong> Flag the lowest-scoring share by each score and count how many flagged outputs are really unfaithful. Ties at the cut-off are counted at their expected value under a random tie-break.</p>\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-budget\">\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label class=\"ctl\"><span>Share flagged for review: <span class=\"rangeval\" id=\"bud-val\">20%</span></span><input type=\"range\" id=\"bud\" min=\"5\" max=\"60\" step=\"1\" value=\"20\" aria-describedby=\"bud-val\"></label>\n      <fieldset class=\"ctl\"><legend>Labels</legend>\n        <div class=\"seg\" id=\"bud-label\">\n          <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"bud-label\" value=\"solver\" checked><span>Solver</span></label>\n          <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"bud-label\" value=\"panel\"><span>Panel (weighted)</span></label>\n        </div>\n      </fieldset>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-bud\"></div>\n    <ul class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><li><i style=\"background:var(--accent)\"></i>Peer agreement</li><li><i style=\"background:var(--base)\"></i>LLM judge</li><li><i style=\"background:none;border-top:2px dashed #888;height:0;border-radius:0\"></i>Base rate of unfaithful</li></ul>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"bud-take\"></p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============================ FAILS -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"fails\" aria-labelledby=\"h-fails\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-fails\">Where it fails</h2>\n  <p class=\"prose\">Agreement cannot see a mistake that most peers make. On the fresh set, panel items whose sentence has an unfaithful modal cluster (61 items) drop the score to 0.419 AUROC while the judge holds 0.786. <button class=\"plain\" id=\"go-modebad\" type=\"button\">Show those 61 items in the browser</button></p>\n\n  <div class=\"two\">\n    <div>\n      <h3 id=\"h-dose\">The dose test</h3>\n      <p class=\"question\"><strong>How many shared errors does it take?</strong> On 200 development sentences, <em>k</em> of the eight peers were replaced by renamed copies of a <button class=\"term\" data-term=\"mutant\">mutant</button>. Detection is the probability that the faithful formula scores above the mutant.</p>\n      <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-dose\">\n        <div class=\"controls\">\n          <fieldset class=\"ctl\"><legend>Replacement order</legend>\n            <div class=\"seg\" id=\"dose-order\">\n              <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"dose-order\" value=\"random\" checked><span>Random peers</span></label>\n              <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"dose-order\" value=\"faithful_first\"><span>Faithful peers first</span></label>\n            </div>\n          </fieldset>\n          <label class=\"ctl\"><span>Peers replaced, k = <span class=\"rangeval\" id=\"dose-kval\">2</span></span><input type=\"range\" id=\"dose-k\" min=\"0\" max=\"8\" step=\"2\" value=\"2\" aria-describedby=\"dose-kval\"></label>\n        </div>\n        <div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-dose\"></div>\n        <ul class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><li><i style=\"background:var(--accent)\"></i>Detection, pooled over 560 items (95% interval)</li><li><i style=\"background:none;border-top:2px dashed #888;height:0;border-radius:0\"></i>Chance</li></ul>\n        <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"dose-take\"></p>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n    <div>\n      <h3 id=\"h-legal\">Long legal definitions</h3>\n      <p class=\"question\"><strong>Does it survive text rich in exceptions?</strong> Weighted AUROC on 655 legal candidates labelled by the panel from the sentence alone, by count of exception and condition markers.</p>\n      <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-legal\">\n        <div role=\"tablist\" aria-label=\"Marker bin\" id=\"lg-tabs\"></div>\n        <div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-legal\"></div>\n        <ul class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><li><i style=\"background:var(--accent)\"></i>Peer agreement</li><li><i style=\"background:var(--base)\"></i>LLM judges</li><li><i style=\"background:var(--other)\"></i>Other reference-free scores</li></ul>\n        <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"lg-take\"></p>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n\n  <h3 id=\"h-real\">Shared error in real development data</h3>\n  <p class=\"question prose\"><strong>Does the dose curve show up without constructed mutants?</strong> <button class=\"term\" data-term=\"conc\">Concordance within sentences</button> of the agreement score, by the share of peer weight held by clusters with the wrong meaning (6,772 faithful × unfaithful pairs in 508 development sentences).</p>\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-real\">\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-real\"></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"real-take\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <h3>What the paper does not show</h3>\n  <ul class=\"limits\">\n    <li><strong>Thin increment.</strong> Under panel labels the gain over judge, roundtrip and structural scores is +0.033 with a 95% interval of [−0.001, 0.066]. It is significant only under a directional test, and the fresh panel has 256 items (Kish effective sample size 202).</li>\n    <li><strong>No gain over an existing estimator.</strong> Peer agreement does not beat binary Dawid–Skene agreement on panel labels (−0.003), and its gain over majority clustering comes from reliability weighting.</li>\n    <li><strong>LLM labels.</strong> Panel labels are LLM judgments, with Cohen κ = 0.57 against human corrections on MALLS. No human adjudication was used. On legal text κ falls to 0.17 on sentences with four or more markers.</li>\n    <li><strong>Substituted and missing baselines.</strong> Roundtrip baselines on the fresh and legal sets used a local Qwen3-8B back-translation. The frontier judge was not run on fresh items. GenV, FormalAlign and the relabelling framework of Brunello et al. were not benchmarked.</li>\n    <li><strong>Operating conditions.</strong> The score needs several independent systems per sentence and cannot score a lone output beyond what self-consistency gives (0.842 against 0.843 on fresh panel items).</li>\n    <li><strong>Signal between sentences.</strong> On development solver labels, shuffling labels within sentences leaves the score at 0.70 AUROC against a true 0.82, so much of its item-level AUROC separates easy from hard sentences.</li>\n    <li><strong>Error types.</strong> No reference-free method in the study named real error types better than always predicting the most frequent type; the strength profile named the panel's primary error for 12.2% of fresh unfaithful items against 25.5% for always answering \"added condition\".</li>\n  </ul>\n</div>\n</section>\n</main>\n\n<!-- ============================ FOOTER -->\n<footer id=\"sources\" aria-labelledby=\"h-sources\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-sources\">Sources and glossary</h2>\n  <ul class=\"links\" aria-label=\"Paper links (footer)\">\n    <li><a class=\"btn primary\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-abf543-do-sentence-and-formula-generalize-the@fork/run_TGmg0LeEY5Gp/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a></li>\n    <li><a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-abf543-do-sentence-and-formula-generalize-the@fork/run_TGmg0LeEY5Gp/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a></li>\n    <li><a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-abf543-do-sentence-and-formula-generalize-the/tree/fork/run_TGmg0LeEY5Gp\">Code repository</a></li>\n  </ul>\n\n  <h3>Data provenance</h3>\n  <ul class=\"prov\">\n    <li><strong>The finding, the item browser, complexity strata, the flag-budget view:</strong> <code>experiment_3/full_method_out.json</code> (4,050 fresh greedy outputs: formulas, recorded scores, solver status, panel label and raked weight, complexity features), with binary Dawid–Skene scores at full precision from <code>experiment_3/results/scores.jsonl</code>. Fields not used by a view were dropped.</li>\n    <li><strong>How it works and Try it:</strong> per-sentence 9 × 9 solver relations rebuilt from <code>experiment_3/work/pair_cache.jsonl</code> and <code>experiment_3/work/fresh_frame.jsonl</code> with the frozen configuration (bijection and partial map, no granularity definitions), and the fitted system weights from <code>experiment_3/work/fresh_dc_weights.json</code>. Recomputing the score from these relations reproduces the recorded score for <span id=\"prov-match\">4,034 of 4,050</span> outputs; the rest sit in three sentences whose pairs are missing from the saved cache.</li>\n    <li><strong>Vocabulary renderings, the dose test, shared error in real data:</strong> <code>experiment_4/results/m1_confound.json</code> and <code>experiment_4/results/m3_boundary.json</code> (aggregates as recorded).</li>\n    <li><strong>Long legal definitions:</strong> <code>experiment_5/results/tests.json</code> (tests X1 and X3, aggregates as recorded).</li>\n  </ul>\n  <p class=\"small muted\">Every number in the prose is taken from the paper. Every number in a view is computed from, or copied from, the file named above.</p>\n\n  <h3 id=\"h-gloss\">Glossary</h3>\n  <dl class=\"gloss\" id=\"gloss\"></dl>\n</div>\n</footer>\n\n<div id=\"tip\" role=\"status\" aria-live=\"polite\"></div>\n<div id=\"termtip\" role=\"tooltip\"></div>\n\n<!--DATA-->\n\n<script>\n(function(){\n\"use strict\";\nvar $ = function(s, r){ return (r||document).querySelector(s); };\nvar $$ = function(s, r){ return Array.prototype.slice.call((r||document).querySelectorAll(s)); };\nfunction J(id){ return JSON.parse(document.getElementById(id).textContent); }\nvar D = J(\"data-items\"), PEERS = J(\"data-peers\"), EX = J(\"data-example\"), E4 = J(\"data-exp4\"), LEGAL = J(\"data-legal\");\nvar SYS = D.systems, SENTS = D.sentences, ITEMS = D.items;\nvar SHORT = {\"gpt-4.1-mini\":\"gpt-4.1-mini\",\"gpt-oss-120b\":\"gpt-oss-120b\",\"gemini-2.5-flash\":\"gemini-2.5-flash\",\"mistral-small-3.2-24b\":\"mistral-small-3.2\",\"gemma-3-27b\":\"gemma-3-27b\",\"deepseek-v3.1\":\"deepseek-v3.1\",\"phi-4\":\"phi-4\",\"qwen-2.5-7b\":\"qwen-2.5-7b\",\"llama-3.1-8b\":\"llama-3.1-8b\"};\nvar REL = {E:\"EQUIV\",S:\"STRONGER\",W:\"WEAKER\",I:\"INCOMPARABLE\",C:\"CONTRADICTORY\",U:\"UNALIGNABLE\",\"?\":\"missing from cache\",\"-\":\"n/a\"};\nvar CORPUS = {malls:\"MALLS\",folio:\"FOLIO\",proverqa:\"ProverQA\"};\nvar SVGNS = \"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\";\nvar reduce = window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia(\"(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)\").matches;\nITEMS.forEach(function(it, i){ it.i = i; });\n\n/* ---------------- helpers */\nfunction esc(s){ return String(s == null ? ws[i] : 1; if (ys[i] === 1) Wp += w; else Wn += w; }\n  if (!Wp || !Wn) return null;\n  idx.sort(function(a, b){ return xs[a] - xs[b]; });\n  var acc = 0, below = 0, k = 0;\n  while (k < idx.length){\n    var j = k, tp = 0, tn = 0, v = xs[idx[k]];\n    while (j < idx.length && xs[idx[j]] === v){ var ww = ws ? ws[idx[j]] : 1; if (ys[idx[j]] === 1) tp += ww; else tn += ww; j++; }\n    acc += tp * (below + 0.5 * tn); below += tn; k = j;\n  }\n  return acc / (Wp * Wn);\n}\nfunction aucOf(rows, key, fam){\n  var ys = [], xs = [], ws = [];\n  rows.forEach(function(r){\n    var y = fam === \"panel\" ? ### [166] ASSISTANT · 2026-09-24 17:22:08 UTC

```
I've built `interactive.html`, an explorable page of about 1.4 MB with no network loads. Every chart is recomputed in the browser from the run's recorded per-item scores and labels, and it reproduces the paper's headline numbers. I operated every control in headless Chromium at 390 px and 1440 px: the console showed no messages and the page never scrolled sideways.

**What the page shows:**
- **The finding:** a bar chart of AUROC for peer agreement, the LLM judge (the baseline) and six other scores. You can switch between panel and solver labels and pick a subset. It gives 0.827 and 0.874 against the judge's 0.791 and 0.727. On the 61 items where most systems share an error, the score drops to 0.419 while the judge holds 0.786.
- **How it works:** a six-stage stepper that walks one real sentence ("All customers in James' family who subscribe to HBO services…") through the method. It uses the maps, relations, clusters and weights recorded for that sentence and ends with the score arithmetic: 1.772 / 2.771 = 0.639, the same as the recorded score.
- **Explore the evidence:**
  - a browser over all 4,050 outputs, with filters and a detail panel that puts the sentence, the candidate formula, the audited gold, the score, the judge, both labels and each peer relation side by side;
  - tabs by complexity feature, which match the paper's Figure 5 exactly;
  - tabs by vocabulary rendering.
- **Try it:** an exact live recomputation of the score for any of the 450 sentences, where you can remove peers or switch to uniform weights. A second slider sets the share of outputs flagged for review and compares how many of the flagged outputs are really unfaithful under the score versus the judge.
- **Where it fails:** the dose test (how detection falls as more peers share the error), the legal-text results by marker count, a real-data chart of how the score degrades as wrong-meaning peers gain weight, and the paper's limitations.
- **Footer:** all three links, which file each view comes from, and a glossary of 16 terms that also appear as tooltips.

**Things you should know:**
- **16 outputs don't recompute.** Rebuilding the score from the saved solver relations gives the recorded value for 4,034 of the 4,050 outputs. The other 16 are in three sentences whose pairs are missing from the saved cache. The page says so.
- **One column comes from a second file.** Binary Dawid–Skene agreement comes out at 0.828 from the main output file, because its scores are rounded to six decimals. I took that one column at full precision from `scores.jsonl`, which gives the paper's 0.830.
- **No author line or citation.** The paper has neither, so the page shows neither rather than making one up.
- **`index.html` needed no change.** It already linked to `interactive.html` in its hero and footer, so I left it alone.
- **I edited one line of `README.md`.** It said the page references no other file, which is no longer true because the page shows the method diagram (`figures/fig2_v0.jpg`). That is the only image on the page.

All prose numbers appear in `paper.tex`, and the prose has no banned words, em dashes or hedges. The three paper, report and code links match the given URLs character for character. The extraction and build scripts and all screenshots are in the scratchpad, outside the published folder.

Files are in the paper folder:
- `interactive.html`
- `.terminal_claude_agent_struct_out.json`
```
